subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden mixed trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` suppression, and what boundary should separate internal silent-intent text from legitimate substantive replies that mention or append the token?
rationale: Current main deliberately preserves some substantive trailing-token replies, while the issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; that is a shared security and message-delivery contract choice.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define shared silent-intent detection that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies across delivery paths.

options.title: Use blanket trailing suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY`, accepting that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-wrapped, JSON, and reasoning-prefixed silent payloads are suppressed, then retarget or close broad suppression requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define shared silent-intent detection that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies across delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the shared reply contract introduced by the PR 31080 landing and needs a maintainer-level security/product boundary call.
